rule.description: responsibility-saturated-class: a class declaring at least 12 methods in its own body whose state-using methods decompose into at least 3 maximal groups that share self/cls data attributes within a group and none across groups (at least 2 methods per group). Each qualifying group is one responsibility the class bundles with unrelated others; accesses to names that are themselves declared methods count as method calls, not shared state.

checks.description: Detect a class that bundles several mutually unrelated stateful duties under one roof.
checks.detected_relation: class-with-many-own-body-methods -> set of maximal method groups bound by disjoint self/cls data attributes
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The grammar container at the center of rule construction has accreted registries and policies that share no state with each other or with the rule map it was built to hold; every added duty drags in its own private state island, so the class changes for unrelated reasons.

matches.evidence: Rule-map responsibility, the class's original duty: methods __init__, __str__, _check_default_rule, _copy, match and parse all read or write the default_rule attribute and touch no attribute of any other responsibility group.

Custom-callable classification absorbed from the deleted module-level factory: _init_custom_rule_forms and _custom_rule_form share the per-grammar cache _custom_rule_forms, which decides and remembers the 2-argument versus 5-argument form of each callable rule; the wrapping method _wrap_custom_rule grew from the same absorbed factory.

String-literal evaluation and grammar-wide type policing absorbed from the deleted utils helper and from the visitor's own instance state: _init_literal_registry and make_literal share _last_literal_node_and_type, the accumulate-and-refuse record that keeps every literal in one grammar the same type. The rule-tree builders were re-threaded to route through it: RuleVisitor stores the grammar back-reference at construction (E2), visit_spaceless_literal delegates literal construction to the grammar and lazily spins one up when detached (E3), and BootstrappingGrammar hands itself to the visitor during the two-level bootstrap (E7).

Token-grammar bookkeeping and token-mode policy: _init_token_types and make_token_matcher share the token-type ledger _known_token_types, and check_token_regex_support carries the token-mode policy that regexes cannot match pre-lexed tokens. The token construction path was re-threaded through the grammar: TokenGrammar passes itself into the token rule visitor (E6), and the visitor's literal (E4) and regex (E5) hooks delegate to the grammar instead of acting on their own.

Rule-string registration and decorator-grammar assembly absorbed from the visitor metaclass and the decorator: the class-level registry _rule_method_syntaxes is written by tag_rule_method and read by from_rule_methods. The rule decorator now delegates tagging to the grammar (E9) and the metaclass delegates default-grammar assembly to it (E8), replacing the rule-string bookkeeping previously carried on each method alone.

excluded.reason: A sizable visitor with many visit hooks, but they share only the traversal inputs (custom_rules and the grammar back-reference) while coordinating a single tree-walking concern; it forms fewer than three disjoint state groups and is not flagged.
Overrides two visit hooks of RuleVisitor and adds no state of its own; it routes to the saturated owner instead of accumulating regions.
Subclasses whose own bodies are thin construction overrides; inherited members are invisible to the rule, and their own bodies do not approach the method threshold.
The generic visitation shell: a handful of methods over one traversal concern, with no second disjoint state region.
Matching-node duties that already cohere on expression state; a plain big class by method count does not qualify unless its state regions decompose.
